newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly should be aware of the consequences if its draft is too radical, PM's Office Minister Pokin Polakul warns. The political reform process is highly contentious, with all sides taking firm but often conflicting positions, says Pokin, chairman of the Campaign for Political Reform Subcommittee. (BANGKOK POST)

- The son of an influential tycoon is charged with attempted murder following the shooting and beating up of an ambassador's nephew at a Bangkok pub early on Tuesday. Man Kong-udom, whose father owns Siam Rath newspaper, is among 10 others accused of assaulting Assadangmongkol Tantemsap, nephew of the ambassador to China, at the pub. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark, who was last seen in Bangkok, is now missing, and speculation is rife that he may still be somewhere in Thailand. The 29-year-old prince, who arrived on a semi-official visit on May 13, was supposed to leave last Friday after an audience with Their Majesties the King and Queen the night before. (BANGKOK POST)

- Debt-ridden Finance One Plc has revealed its blueprint for survival but analysts and investors say they remain worry. The announcement of far-reaching plans to restructure Finance One's subsidiaries and debts comes as the Stock Exchange of Thailand braces itself for a resumption of trading in the firm's shares tomorrow. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The Southern Seaboard Development Committee has endorsed the establishment of an Islamic bank to serve Muslim residents in the country's five southernmost provinces. The Government Savings Bank, which has been promoting the idea, will be the core partner in the venture. (BANGKOK POST)
